wallpapers.title: WARTY COMB JELLY
wallpapers.line1: Mnemiopsis leidyi, the sea walnut. Light breaks into rainbows on its comb rows, which glow blue-green when disturbed.
wallpapers.line2: 23 February 2013  ·  Photo: Bruno C. Vellutini  ·  CC BY-SA 3.0

wallpapers.title: WHITE-SPOTTED JELLYFISH
wallpapers.line1: Phyllorhiza punctata under blue light, every white spot lit. Native to the western Pacific, from Australia to Japan.
wallpapers.line2: 26 February 2018  ·  Photo: Alexander Svensson (Flickr)  ·  CC BY 2.0

wallpapers.title: GOLDEN JELLIES
wallpapers.line1: Jellyfish glowing gold against black water. The photographer called them sea gold.
wallpapers.line2: 9 July 2019  ·  Photo: Andrey Biksaleev  ·  CC BY 4.0

wallpapers.title: JAPANESE SEA NETTLE
wallpapers.line1: Chrysaora pacifica at the Vancouver Aquarium. It lives in the northwest Pacific, from Japan and Korea to China.
wallpapers.line2: 18 January 2015  ·  Photo: Paul Harrison  ·  CC BY-SA 4.0

wallpapers.title: MOON JELLYFISH
wallpapers.line1: Aurelia aurita in Åbyfjorden, Sweden, about 12 cm across. The four rings are its gonads, seen through the bell.

wallpapers.title: DEEP-SEA ISOPOD
wallpapers.line1: Brucerolis brandtae, about 5 cm long, brought up from just over 900 m deep off the east coast of New Zealand.
wallpapers.line2: 6 February 2014  ·  Photo: Peter Marriott, NIWA  ·  CC BY 4.0

wallpapers.title: LION'S MANE JELLYFISH
wallpapers.line1: Cyanea capillata in Gullmarn fjord, Sweden: one of the largest jellyfish known. This one is 10–12 cm across.

wallpapers.title: WHITE-SPOTTED JELLYFISH
wallpapers.line1: The spotted bell of Phyllorhiza punctata up close, at Tiergarten Schönbrunn in Vienna.
wallpapers.line2: 24 July 2020  ·  Photo: Johannes Maximilian  ·  CC BY-SA 4.0

wallpapers.title: MONTEREY JELLIES
wallpapers.line1: Jellyfish trailing their frilled arms through the blue of the Monterey Bay Aquarium, California.
wallpapers.line2: 11 October 2018  ·  Photo: Pedro Szekely (Flickr)  ·  CC BY-SA 2.0

wallpapers.title: HARP COMB JELLY
wallpapers.line1: Lyrocteis imperatoris, a comb jelly up to 15 cm tall, shaped like a lyre, that lives on the sea floor. Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium.

wallpapers.title: BLUEFIRE JELLYFISH
wallpapers.line1: Cyanea lamarckii in Brofjorden, Sweden, pulled in tight to swim. Its bell grows to about 10–20 cm.

wallpapers.title: CAUGHT
wallpapers.line1: Three moon jellyfish caught by a young lion's mane, which will eat them one by one. Rågårdsdal, Sweden.
